taiwan_invasion.name: China Invades Taiwan
taiwan_invasion.description: Full-scale Chinese military operation against Taiwan, triggering TSMC production shutdown, US-China decoupling, and global supply chain disruption.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2011 Thai floods disrupted HDD supply for 6+ months; TSMC is 10x more critical
transmission_channels.description: TSMC produces ~90% of advanced semiconductors. A military conflict would halt production, creating a global chip famine lasting 12-24 months.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2018-19 US-China trade war caused 15-20% drawdowns in exposed sectors
transmission_channels.description: Immediate sanctions, export controls, and asset freezes would sever remaining US-China economic ties.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 1990 Gulf War oil spike (+70% in 3 months)
transmission_channels.description: Taiwan Strait shipping disruption affects ~40% of global container traffic, spiking energy and shipping costs.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: Feb 2022 Russia-Ukraine: S&P 500 dropped 11% in first month
transmission_channels.description: Global flight to safety — US Treasuries, gold, and JPY surge; emerging market assets collapse.

rate_shock_up.name: Fed Rate Shock +200bp
rate_shock_up.description: Federal Reserve forced to raise rates by 200bp due to inflation resurgence, repricing all duration-sensitive assets.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2022 rate hiking cycle: Nasdaq fell 33%, long-duration growth stocks worst hit
transmission_channels.description: Higher discount rates disproportionately compress valuations of high-growth, long-duration equities.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2006-07 rate hikes preceded 2008 credit crisis
transmission_channels.description: Higher rates increase borrowing costs, stress leveraged balance sheets, and widen credit spreads.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2022: 30yr mortgage rates doubled, existing home sales fell 35%
transmission_channels.description: Mortgage rates spike, reducing housing affordability and construction activity.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2013 Taper Tantrum: EM equities fell 15% in 3 months
transmission_channels.description: Higher US rates attract global capital, strengthening USD and pressuring emerging markets.

us_recession.name: US Recession
us_recession.description: Standard US recession with GDP contracting 2-3%, unemployment rising to 6-7%, earnings declining 15-20%.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2001 recession: S&P 500 earnings fell 30%; 2008: fell 45%
transmission_channels.description: Corporate profits decline as consumer spending and business investment contract.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2008-09: high yield spreads widened from 300bp to 2100bp
transmission_channels.description: Rising defaults and wider spreads pressure leveraged companies and financial institutions.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2008-09: consumer spending fell 3.3%, worst since WWII
transmission_channels.description: Rising unemployment and declining confidence reduce discretionary spending.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: Avg recession P/E contraction: 20-30% from peak
transmission_channels.description: Forward P/E multiples compress as growth expectations are revised downward.

us_recession_severe.name: US Severe Recession / Financial Crisis
us_recession_severe.description: 2008-level financial crisis: GDP contracts 5%+, unemployment exceeds 10%, systemic bank stress, equity markets down 40-50%.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2008: Lehman collapse froze interbank lending, LIBOR-OIS spread hit 364bp
transmission_channels.description: Banking system stress causes credit markets to seize, cutting off corporate funding.
Deep recession causes severe corporate earnings decline across all sectors.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2008-09: US household wealth fell $13 trillion
transmission_channels.description: Falling asset prices force margin calls, fund redemptions, and consumer retrenchment.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2008: Crisis spread from US to global banking, EM currencies, and commodities
transmission_channels.description: US financial stress propagates globally through trade, capital flows, and confidence channels.

china_hard_landing.name: China Economic Hard Landing
china_hard_landing.description: China GDP growth collapses to 0-1%, property sector implodes, USD/CNY spikes, global demand shock.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2015-16 China slowdown: global commodities fell 30%, EM currencies lost 15%
transmission_channels.description: China represents 18% of global GDP. Sharp slowdown reduces demand for commodities, luxury goods, and tech hardware.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2020 COVID lockdowns disrupted Chinese manufacturing for months
transmission_channels.description: Economic distress may disrupt Chinese manufacturing and supply chains for global companies.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2015: iron ore fell 40%, copper fell 25% on China slowdown fears
transmission_channels.description: China consumes 50%+ of industrial metals. Demand collapse crashes commodity prices.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2015-16: China burned $800B in reserves defending CNY
transmission_channels.description: CNY devaluation pressures EM currencies and increases FX volatility for exposed companies.

ai_bubble_burst.name: AI Capex Bubble Bursts
ai_bubble_burst.description: AI monetization disappoints expectations. Hyperscaler capex cuts 40%+, GPU demand collapses, AI-adjacent stocks reprice sharply.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2000-01 telecom capex bust: equipment makers lost 80-95% of value
transmission_channels.description: Hyperscalers (MSFT, GOOG, META, AMZN) slash GPU/datacenter spending as AI ROI disappoints.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2000 dot-com: Cisco fell 86%, Intel fell 75% on capex cycle reversal
transmission_channels.description: NVDA, AMD, and supply chain face severe demand cliff as data center GPU orders evaporate.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2022: high-growth tech multiples compressed 60-80%
transmission_channels.description: Market reprices AI-beneficiary stocks from growth to value multiples.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2000: Nasdaq decline spread from pure-play internet to all tech
transmission_channels.description: Sentiment shift drags down broader technology sector regardless of direct AI exposure.

oil_shock.name: Major Middle East Oil Shock
oil_shock.description: Major disruption to Middle East oil production (Iran-Saudi conflict, Strait of Hormuz closure). Oil spikes to $150+/barrel.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 1973 OPEC embargo: oil quadrupled, triggering global recession
transmission_channels.description: Oil above $150/bbl raises input costs for transportation, manufacturing, and consumer goods.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 1979-80: oil shock pushed US CPI above 14%, forcing aggressive Fed hikes
transmission_channels.description: Energy price spike reignites inflation, forcing central banks to tighten despite slowing growth.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2008 $147 oil: consumer confidence index fell to record lows
transmission_channels.description: Higher gasoline and heating costs reduce discretionary spending power.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2022 Russia-Ukraine: oil rose 40%, VIX spiked, defense stocks rallied
transmission_channels.description: Broader geopolitical uncertainty increases risk premiums across all asset classes.

pandemic_2.name: Pandemic II / Supply Chain Shutdown
pandemic_2.description: Novel pandemic causes widespread lockdowns and supply chain disruption. Similar to COVID-19 but with lessons learned enabling faster response.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2020 COVID: semiconductor lead times doubled, shipping costs rose 10x
transmission_channels.description: Factory shutdowns and logistics breakdowns create shortages and production delays.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2020 Q2: US GDP fell 31% annualized, worst single quarter on record
transmission_channels.description: Lockdowns and fear devastate services, travel, and discretionary spending.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: March 2020: S&P 500 fell 34% in 23 trading days, VIX hit 82
transmission_channels.description: Panic selling creates liquidity vacuum. Credit markets freeze before central bank intervention.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2020: 2-3 weeks between lockdown announcements and fiscal/monetary response
transmission_channels.description: Markets overshoot downward before massive fiscal and monetary support materializes.

us_debt_crisis.name: US Debt Crisis / Credit Downgrade
us_debt_crisis.description: US debt sustainability questioned. Treasury auction failures, further credit downgrades, 10yr yields spike to 7%+, dollar weakens.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2011 S&P downgrade: S&P 500 fell 17%, VIX doubled, Treasury paradoxically rallied
transmission_channels.description: Failed Treasury auctions or severe buyer strikes spike yields and crash risk-free rate assumptions.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: No direct US precedent; 1992 UK ERM crisis saw 15% GBP drop
transmission_channels.description: Loss of confidence in US fiscal management weakens dollar, raising import costs.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2011 European debt crisis: peripheral spreads widened 500bp+
transmission_channels.description: Rising sovereign risk reprices all credit. Corporate borrowing costs spike across the board.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: Post-2022 sanctions: central banks accelerated gold purchases
transmission_channels.description: Foreign central banks reduce USD reserve holdings, structural dollar weakness.

big_tech_antitrust.name: Big Tech Regulatory Breakup
big_tech_antitrust.description: Major antitrust actions force structural separation of 2-3 Big Tech companies. Market-wide tech repricing as regulatory risk premium increases.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 1984 AT&T breakup: stock underperformed for 5 years post-split
transmission_channels.description: Forced separation eliminates cross-subsidization and network effects that drive margins.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2020-21 China tech crackdown: Alibaba fell 75%, sector lost $1.5T
transmission_channels.description: Regulatory uncertainty adds permanent risk premium to all platform businesses.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: S&P 500 top 10 concentration at 35%+ — breakups would force massive rebalancing
transmission_channels.description: Mega-cap breakups reduce index concentration, forcing passive fund rebalancing and selling.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: EU GDPR reduced VC investment in EU adtech by 30%
transmission_channels.description: Regulatory overhang reduces M&A activity and investment in adjacent tech sectors.

usd_crash.name: US Dollar Sharp Decline (-25%)
usd_crash.description: US dollar index (DXY) drops 25% over 6-12 months due to loss of reserve currency confidence, de-dollarization, or twin deficit crisis.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2002-08 dollar decline: import prices rose 30%, contributing to inflation
transmission_channels.description: Weaker dollar raises cost of imported goods, squeezing margins for importers and consumers.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: S&P 500 gets ~40% of revenue abroad; weak USD historically boosts reported earnings
transmission_channels.description: Companies with high international revenue benefit from translation effects, partially offsetting macro drag.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: Dollar-denominated commodities historically move inverse to DXY
transmission_channels.description: Dollar-denominated commodity prices rise, benefiting producers but hurting consumers.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 1985 Plaza Accord triggered 50% dollar decline over 2 years
transmission_channels.description: Foreign investors reduce US asset holdings, creating selling pressure on equities and bonds.

russia_nato.name: Russia-NATO Military Escalation
russia_nato.description: Russia-NATO conflict escalates beyond Ukraine. Article 5 invoked, direct military confrontation, risk of tactical nuclear weapon use.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2022: Russian gas cutoff sent EU natural gas prices up 10x, triggered recession fears
transmission_channels.description: Complete Russian energy cutoff to Europe spikes global energy prices and triggers EU recession.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis: S&P 500 fell 7% in a week, recovered quickly after resolution
transmission_channels.description: Even low-probability nuclear escalation creates extreme risk aversion and flight to safety.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2022-25: EU defense spending increased 30%+ following Ukraine invasion
transmission_channels.description: NATO countries dramatically increase defense budgets, benefiting defense contractors.

transmission_channels.historical_analogue: 2022 Russia sanctions: G7 froze $300B in Russian reserves, trade rerouted
transmission_channels.description: Expanded sanctions, trade route disruptions, and commodity supply shocks.
